name: fine-tuned_movie_retriever-all-mpnet-base-v2
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2 (config.json max_position_embeddings 514). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: bidirectional encoder (MPNet), full attention, no causal mask, relative position bias
notes: ADDED 2026-11-01. Fine-tune for movie/TV retrieval on ~32K synthetic (query, positive, negative) triplets with MNRL, 4 epochs. Recorded because the card prints 'Fine-Tuned Model Score' and 'Base Model Score' as two columns of one table on 3,598 held-out queries: Recall@1 0.159 -> 0.459, Recall@3 0.289 -> 0.695, Recall@5 0.342 -> 0.765, Recall@10 0.425 -> 0.836, MRR 0.251 -> 0.598. The base identity is inconsistent on the card and this is the reason to hold confidence down: the base_model tag and config.json (architectures: MPNetModel) both say all-mpnet-base-v2, the Training Details text says BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5, and the table column is only labelled 'Base Model Score'. The record uses mpnet, matching the hosted weights' architecture. Evaluated on the author's own synthetic-query distribution, so this is in-domain retrieval lift.

benchmarks.name: Recall@1 (movie metadata + vibe queries, 3,598 held-out)
benchmarks.config: Card table '| Metric | Fine-Tuned Model Score | Base Model Score |': base 0.159 vs fine-tuned 0.459 on 3,598 held-out metadata/vibe queries, top-k cosine similarity, MultipleNegativesRankingLoss 4 epochs on ~32K synthetic triplets. IDENTITY WARNING: the card's Training Details says the base is BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 while the repo's base_model tag says all-mpnet-base-v2 and config.json architectures says MPNetModel - the column header only says 'Base Model Score', so which 110M base produced 0.159 is unstated.
